doc.title: David Friesen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2024

title: Kyle Gordon's orchestration and goodbyes
summary: Friesen credits orchestrator Kyle Gordon for the album, then they say farewell and mention East Coast ties.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Okay. Yeah. Well listen I did not orchestrate that music. I composed all the music, I did some of the arrangements. The orchestration was done by Kyle Gordon, who was one of I think five orchestrators for the Oppenheimer film that won an Academy Award. He’s a young — he’s not so young — but yeah, everyone is younger than me. My dad always told me, “Son, always have respect for your elders” but I’m finding it more difficult all the time finding anyone older. But anyways, he’s a great young orchestrator, a graduate of UNT — University of North Texas, which has a great jazz program as you know. And so he did the orchestrations for that, and he did such a great job.
Yeah. It’s been a pleasure. I appreciate you wanting to interview me. Did we get everything? We got it all done?
Yes, we got it. And I hope that someday you get in my neck of the woods so I can hear you perform live.

Yes. I will definitely let you know when I’m on the — usually I’m flying over you on my way to Europe. I spent many years and a lot of time in New York and it’s such a great — the East Coast — it’s a great place to be, I wish I could be there more it just doesn’t work out right now.
